text: An often-overlooked issue with NSAID consumption in combination with resistance training, however, is the potential interference with muscular adaptations. In addition to the effects of NSAIDs on pain sensation, prostanoids also are purported to stimulate the upstream regulators of protein synthesis, including PI3K and extracellular signal-regulated kinases (79, 208, 228). Moreover, there is evidence that prostanoids are intricately involved in enhancing satellite cell proliferation, differentiation, and fusion (21), thereby facilitating greater muscle protein accretion (115). These data provide compelling evidence that COX enzymes are important and perhaps even necessary for maximizing resistance training-induced muscle hypertrophy (256).
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
